statements.label: Abstract: conditional regularity-degree claim
statements.verbatim: Under a first fall degree assumption the regularity degree of the system is at most 4. Extensive experimental data which supports the assumption is provided.
statements.quantifier_order: Unquantified front-matter statement about 'the system'; no range over n, m, t, V, B or z is given.
statements.notes: Correctly flags the conditionality ('Under a first fall degree assumption'), unlike ST-02.

statements.label: Introduction: 'The first fall degree is proved to be 4.'
statements.verbatim: The system incorporates more variables than previously but has algebraic degree only 3. The first fall degree is proved to be 4. Then a first fall degree assumption says the regularity degree dF4 of the Grobner basis algorithm F4 is at most 4 as well. The assumption was endorsed by numerous experiments with MAGMA.
statements.quantity: first fall degree (d_ff) of the system, under the paper's own Section 4.4 definition, which is the TRUE degree (no field equations)
statements.quantifier_order: System-level and unhedged: reads as 'for every instance of the system, d_ff = 4'. No exception for the terminal equation and no exception at t = 2.
statements.what_backs_it_in_this_paper: ST-09 proves the fall for the NON-TERMINAL links only, and computes the FAKE (multilinear) degree, not the true degree of the Section 4.4 definition. ST-10 covers the terminal equation experimentally. Nothing covers t = 2.
statements.notes: This is the reading Nagao's Proposition 2 imports, because Proposition 2 is a system-level statement. It is stronger than what the body asserts at ST-11.

statements.label: Introduction: FIPS curves theoretically broken for n > 310
statements.verbatim: Our analysis suggests a number of FIPS binary elliptic curves in [7] are theoretically broken (in case dF4 <= 4) as the new method starts to perform better than Pollard's for n > 310.
statements.what_backs_it_in_this_paper: ST-16 (Section 4.5.2 and Table 3), which rests on ST-12.
statements.notes: Drawn at n = 409, 571 and m = 11, 12 (see :379-386), roughly 20x in n and 2x in m outside the parameter range of the supporting experiments ST-13.

statements.label: Section 4.2: definition of system (5) and its t = 2 degenerate case
statements.verbatim: S3(u1, x1, x2) = 0, S3(ui, ui+1, xi+2) = 0, 1 <= i <= t-3, S3(ut-2, xt, RX) = 0. (5) ... For t = 2 the system consists of only one equation S3(x1, x2, RX) = 0.
statements.quantity: the object every later degree claim is about
statements.notes: System (5) has t-1 equations, exactly one of which (the last) is terminal in R_X. This is the arithmetic that makes ST-11's 't-2' an exact coverage gap of one equation, and empty at t = 2.

statements.label: Section 4.3: success-probability model, equation (11)
statements.verbatim: We adopt the following model. For random z the mapping x1, ..., xt -> St+1(x1, ..., xt, z) is a symmetric random mapping from V^t to Fq.
statements.quantity: P(q, m, t, |V|), probability that a decomposition system is satisfiable
statements.quantifier_order: 'For random z' -- a typical-instance model, stated as such.
statements.notes: Recorded in inputs/SEMAEV-2015-310/source_record.yaml as HEUR-SEMAEV-2015-4.3, consumed by GOAL-RELN-001 and GOAL-ICEX-001. Enumerated here only to rule it out as this campaign's consumed statement.

statements.label: Section 4.4: definition of the first fall degree
statements.verbatim: The first fall degree for (12) is the smallest total degree d_ff such that there exist polynomials g_i = g_i(x_1, ..., x_n), (1 <= i <= m) with max_i(deg g_i + deg f_i) = d_ff, deg(sum_i g_i f_i) < d_ff and sum_i g_i f_i != 0.
statements.quantity: d_ff, defined for the system (12) over a field K
statements.notes: Two features matter downstream. (a) It is stated for (12) = {f_1,...,f_m} with NO field equations adjoined, i.e. it is the TRUE first fall degree in Nagao's taxonomy (NAGAO-2015-984 Definition 5, :398-410) -- whereas ST-09 computes deg_F2 of multilinear coordinate functions, i.e. the FAKE degree (Nagao Definition 6, :430-448). (b) The condition is max_i(deg g_i + deg f_i), a SUM OF DEGREES, with EQUALITY; Nagao's Definition 5 uses max_i{deg(g_i f_i)}, the DEGREE OF THE PRODUCT, with '>='. In a multilinear ring these can differ. Both recovered at glyph level; see reextract.md F-2.

statements.label: Section 4.4: the first fall degree assumption, with its own disclaimer
statements.verbatim: A first fall degree assumption says dF4 <= d_ff and that is a basis for asymptotical complexity estimates in [19]. Although not generally correct, the assumption appears correct for the polynomial systems coming from (4) and was supported by extensive experiments for relatively small parameters in [19, 28]. This is very likely correct for (5) as well, see sections below.
statements.quantifier_order: Hedged twice: 'Although not generally correct' and 'very likely correct for (5) as well'.
statements.what_backs_it_in_this_paper: For (4): experiments in [19, 28], not opened by this task. For (5): 'very likely', plus ST-13/ST-14.
statements.notes: The disclaimer is to the paper's credit and is NOT carried into ST-02. ST-15 shows the assumption is not merely 'not generally correct' in the abstract but is reported false by this paper's own experiments on this paper's own family of systems, one parameter step away.

statements.label: Section 4.5: imported bound m^2 + 1 for the S_{m+1} descent
statements.verbatim: Also it was observed in [19] and proved in [11] that the first fall degree of the Boolean equations coming from S_{m+1}(x_1, ..., x_m, RX) = 0 is at most m^2 + 1.
statements.quantity: first fall degree of the m-th summation-polynomial descent
statements.notes: [11] and [19] were NOT opened by this task. Reported here only as what 2015/310 says about them. This is the baseline the number 4 improves on at m = 2.

statements.label: Section 4.5: THE ARGUMENT. The degree fall for the non-terminal links.
statements.verbatim: We consider the case m = 2 in more detail now. First we take the polynomial (14), where all x1, x2, x3 are variables in V or F2n. Following an idea in [19] it is easy to prove that the first fall degree is 4 in this case. Really, coordinate Boolean functions which represent S3(x1,x2,x3) are of total degree 3. We denote that fact deg_F2 S3(x1,x2,x3) = 3. However deg_F2 x1 S3(x1,x2,x3) = 3 again because x1 S3(x1,x2,x3) = x1[(x1x2 + x1x3 + x2x3)^2 + x1x2x3 + B] = x1^3 x2^2 + x1^3 x3^2 + x1 x2^2 x3^2 + x1^2 x2 x3 + B x1 despite deg_F2 x1 + deg_F2 S3(x1,x2,x3) = 4.
statements.quantity: FAKE (multilinear Boolean) first fall degree of the non-terminal links of (5)
statements.quantifier_order: STRONGEST AVAILABLE: for all n, for all V (subspace or coset), for all curve parameter B, for all non-terminal links, there EXISTS a fall at degree 4 exhibited by ONE FIXED WITNESS -- the variable x1. Not a per-instance witness dressed as a uniform one.
statements.what_backs_it_in_this_paper: Complete as given, for what it covers.
statements.verified_independently: recheck.py RC-1a..e over F_2^5, F_2^7, F_2^9: deg_F2 S3 = 3, deg_F2(x1 S3) = 3 < 1+3 = 4, product nonzero, printed expansion an exact identity. RC-1i supplies the LOWER bound Semaev does not argue -- the degree-3 parts of the n coordinate polynomials of S3 are F2-linearly independent (rank = n at n = 5,7,9), so no constant-multiplier combination falls at degree 3 and the fake first fall degree of that subsystem is EXACTLY 4.
statements.notes: 'the case m = 2' refers to S_{m+1} of the preceding sentence, i.e. S3; it is not a typo for p = 2. See reextract.md reading hazard 1. The whole exhibition reduces to deg_F2(x^a) = popcount(a) (RC-4, verified a = 1..39), a property of the Frobenius. NO PARAMETER k APPEARS IN IT -- that absence is the J-5 control.

statements.label: Section 4.5: the terminal equation, where the argument stops
statements.verbatim: This argument does not work for S3(x1,x2,z), where z is a constant from F2n. We have deg_F2 S3(x1,x2,z) = 2, deg_F2 x1 S3(x1,x2,z) = 3, and deg_F2 x1 + deg_F2 S3(x1,x2,z) = 3. The first fall degree for such polynomials was bounded by 5 in [11]. The experiments show it is always 4 again.
statements.quantity: first fall degree of the terminal link S3(x1, x2, R_X)
statements.quantifier_order: 'always 4 again' -- universal in form, experimental in support.
statements.what_backs_it_in_this_paper: The paper's own experiments only. The argument ST-09 explicitly does not reach here and the paper says so.
statements.verified_independently: recheck.py RC-1f/g/h reproduce all three of Semaev's numbers exactly: with z constant, deg_F2 S3 = 2, deg_F2(x S3) = 3, bound = 1+2 = 3, so there is no fall. RC-3g: no DEGREE-1 monomial multiplier falls below 4. RC-3b..f: the degree-2 field monomials u^3, x u^2, x^2 u and x^3 DO produce a fall at degree 4, so the gap is closable by the paper's own method with a multiplier the paper does not give.
statements.notes: This refusal is a POSITIVE CONTROL on the argument: it discriminates the case it can prove from the case it cannot, which is the behaviour a sound argument should have. Contrast ST-15, where no such discrimination occurs. Separately: Nagao (NAGAO-2015-984 :452-459) attributes the multiplier 'xu' to Semaev for this case; for m = x*u, deg_F2(m*S3) = 4 = the bound 2+2, so there is NO fall (recheck.py RC-3a). The obstruction is the term x^3 u^3, of Boolean degree wt(3)+wt(3) = 4. Flagged, not adjudicated -- that paper's joints are not this task's.

statements.label: Section 4.5: the body's own summary -- 'at least t-2 of the equations'
statements.verbatim: Anyway at least t - 2 of the equations in (5) have the first fall degree 4.
statements.quantifier_order: Universal in t but EXPLICITLY PARTIAL in coverage: t-2 of the t-1 equations of (5).
statements.what_backs_it_in_this_paper: ST-09, which reaches exactly the t-2 non-terminal links.
statements.verified_independently: recheck.py RC-5a/b/c: system (5) has t-1 equations (ST-04), so exactly one -- the terminal S3(u_{t-2}, x_t, R_X) -- is outside the argument at every t; and at t = 2, t-2 = 0, so the sentence covers ZERO equations while Assumption 1's range 2 <= t <= m includes t = 2. RC-5d: the t = 2 support is entirely experimental, six rows of Table 2 at (n,m) = (15,4), (15,5), (16,4), (19,3), (21,3), (40,2).
statements.notes: Materially weaker than ST-02, which is what Nagao imports. The difference between these two is the coverage component of the J-4c gap.

statements.label: Assumption 1
statements.verbatim: Assumption 1. Let q = 2^n and 2 <= m < n, k = ceil(n/m). Also let V be a subspace of dimension k in F2n. Then dF4 <= 4 for a Boolean equation system equivalent to (5) for any 2 <= t <= m.
statements.quantity: d_F4, the F4 regularity degree -- NOT the first fall degree
statements.quantifier_order: Universal over n, over 2 <= m < n, over ANY subspace V of dimension k = ceil(n/m), and over all 2 <= t <= m. It quantifies over the curve parameter B and over R_X NOT AT ALL -- neither appears in the statement.
statements.what_backs_it_in_this_paper: ST-09 + ST-10 + ST-11 for the first fall degree, then ST-07 to cross to d_F4, then ST-13/ST-14 experimentally.
statements.notes: The hypothesis k = ceil(n/m) is load-bearing for the truth of the assumption (see ST-15) and plays NO ROLE WHATEVER in the argument offered for it (see J-5). Separately consumed by GOAL-DREG-001 per provenance.json, not by this campaign.

statements.label: Section 4.5.1: what the experiments actually measure, and on what
statements.verbatim: The system consists of n(t-1) coordinate equations in n(t-2)+kt variables and n(t-2)+kt field equations are added. ... The most important of all the parameters is dF4. We use the verbosity implemented in MAGMA for Faugere's F4. ... 'step degree' is the maximal total degree of the polynomials for which a row echelon form is computed. ... To fill the tables 2300 Boolean systems each of total degree 3 coming from (5), where t = m, were solved.
statements.quantity: d_F4, measured as MAGMA F4 'step degree'
statements.notes: Two consequences. (a) NO EXPERIMENT ANYWHERE IN 2015/310 MEASURES A FIRST FALL DEGREE: Tables 1-2 carry a d_F4 column and no d_ff column, so ST-10's 'The experiments show it is always 4 again' is supported by experiments the paper describes as measuring a different quantity (could_not_determine CND-3). (b) The experiments ADD the n(t-2)+kt field equations, while ST-06's d_ff is defined over the descents alone; adding generators can only lower a first fall degree so the bound still transfers, but it means the assumption ST-07 is never instantiated on one fixed generating set anywhere in the paper (could_not_determine CND-2).

statements.label: Section 4.5.1: the extrapolation sentence
statements.verbatim: We conclude that for all values of n, m and t <= m in the tables Assumption 1 was correct for randomly chosen z in F2n. So the assumption is very likely to be correct for any values of n, m, t <= m.
statements.quantifier_order: THE SLIDE, in one sentence, and it is three slides at once: (1) typical z -> all z, when Assumption 1 quantifies over z not at all; (2) tested (n,m) -> all (n,m) with 2 <= m < n, where tested means n <= 21 plus a single cell at n = 40, with m <= 6, against a FIPS conclusion drawn at n = 409, 571 and m = 11, 12; (3) one V -> any subspace V of dimension k, where the paper itself notes at :540-546 that the choice is not neutral and only two Table 1 rows use a random V, at a single (n,m,k) = (17,3,6).
statements.what_backs_it_in_this_paper: ST-13, i.e. 2300 systems at t = m plus the t < m rows.
statements.notes: The hedge 'very likely' IS present here in the body, and its presence is to the paper's credit. It is absent from ST-02 and from ST-01. Confirmed verbatim at glyph level, reextract.md F-5.

statements.label: Section 4.5.1 closing remark: the regime where the paper reports its own conclusion FALSE
statements.verbatim: To conclude the section we should mention that the maximal degree (regularity degree) generally exceeds 4 when k > ceil(n/m) though the first fall degree is still 4.
statements.quantifier_order: 'generally exceeds' -- the author's report of his own experiments.
statements.what_backs_it_in_this_paper: The paper's own experiments, reported without a table.
statements.role_in_this_read: THE J-5 PROVES-TOO-MUCH OBJECT. On this same family of systems, measured by this same author with this same instrument, the PREMISE of the argument (first fall degree = 4) HOLDS -- he says so -- and the CONCLUSION (d_F4 <= 4) is FALSE -- he says so. Assumption 1 is protected from this only by carrying k = ceil(n/m) among its hypotheses.
statements.notes: Confirmed at glyph level (reextract.md F-4, PDF p.13 y=670/656) because the (cid:100)/(cid:101) ceiling brackets survive the extraction as escapes and the claim turns on reading them correctly.

statements.label: Section 4.5.2: asymptotical complexity under Assumption 1, and Table 3
statements.verbatim: In this section an asymptotical complexity estimate for the discrete logarithm problem in E(F2n) based on Assumption 1 is derived. ... The complexity of solving by the Grobner basis algorithm F4 is [n(m-1)]^{4 omega}.
statements.quantity: time complexity, and the crossover against Pollard rho
statements.quantifier_order: Asymptotic in n, conditional on ST-12.
statements.notes: The exponent 4 in [n(m-1)]^{4 omega} IS d_F4 = 4. This is where Assumption 1 becomes load-bearing for ST-03: the FIPS conclusion needs d_F4 <= 4, which the argument ST-09 does not reach at all -- it reaches only the FAKE first fall degree.

statements.label: Section 4.6: Assumption 2, the weaker route
statements.verbatim: Assumption 2. Let q = 2^n and m = O(sqrt(n/ln n)) for large n, k = ceil(n/m). Also let V be a subspace of dimension k in F2n. Then dF4 = o(sqrt(n/ln n)) for a Boolean equation system equivalent to (5) for any 2 <= t <= m. ... Therefore the asymptotical bound does not depend on any first fall degree assumption. However the complexity estimates in Table 3 will change.
statements.quantity: d_F4, at a much weaker bound
statements.quantifier_order: Same shape as ST-12, with m restricted to O(sqrt(n/ln n)) and the conclusion weakened from <= 4 to o(sqrt(n/ln n)).
statements.what_backs_it_in_this_paper: Stated as an assumption; no argument and no experiment is offered specifically for it.
statements.notes: Recorded because it bounds how much of the paper the J-5 control touches. The asymptotic bound (17) survives on Assumption 2 alone, and Section 4.6 says so; what does not survive without Assumption 1 is Table 3 and therefore ST-03, the FIPS crossover. Note also that ST-15's failure regime is k > ceil(n/m), and Assumption 2 carries the same k = ceil(n/m) hypothesis, so it inherits the same undiscriminated justification.

strongest_claim_the_argument_supports.statement: For every n, every GF(2)-subspace (or coset of one) V in F_2^n, every curve parameter B, and every t >= 3, the descended Boolean system of (5) has FAKE first fall degree at most 4, exhibited by a single uniform witness; and for the non-terminal links taken alone that value is exactly 4.
what_it_excludes: t = 2, where the argument supports nothing at all (ST-11 covers zero equations there).
The terminal equation S3(u_{t-2}, x_t, R_X) at every t (ST-10).

The TRUE first fall degree, reached only by a conversion this paper does not perform (Nagao's Lemma 4, d_F <= d'_F, NAGAO-2015-984 :510-515, of which Nagao says 'Proof of this Lemma is complicated and not constructive').
d_F4, which is what every complexity statement in the paper actually needs, reached only by an assumption the paper itself says is 'not generally correct' (ST-07).
The parameter k. It does not appear in the argument. That absence is J-5.

components.gap: Two conversions separate them and NEITHER IS IN THIS PAPER: fake -> true first fall degree (Nagao's Lemma 4), and d_ff -> d_F4 (ST-07, an assumption the paper says is not generally correct).
components.which_side_must_a_consumer_rely_on: A consumer who wants a bound on the FAKE first fall degree of the descended chained system may rely on the ARGUMENT -- it is sound, uniform, and verified in recheck.py. That is the side H-SEMBIN-a7e721's LINK 1 names. A consumer who wants d_F4 <= 4, which is what ST-03 and ST-16 need, must rely on the STATEMENT, because the argument does not reach it.

components.gap: System (5) has t-1 equations; ST-11 claims t-2. Exactly one equation -- the terminal one -- is outside the argument at every t, and at t = 2 the count is zero while Assumption 1's range includes t = 2.
components.which_side_must_a_consumer_rely_on: A consumer taking the 4 at t = 2, or for the terminal link at any t, relies on the STATEMENT and on the paper's experiments, not on any argument. recheck.py RC-3 shows the terminal gap is closable by the paper's own method with a degree-2 multiplier -- but by the consumer, not by the paper.

components.weight: disclosed in the body, not in the front matter
components.gap: Universal statements, typical-instance evidence: 100 random z per row at n <= 21 (plus one n = 40 cell), m <= 6, one B per table, two rows with a random V -- generalised in one sentence to all n, m, t, z and V, and marked 'very likely'.
components.which_side_must_a_consumer_rely_on: The body discloses the hedge ('very likely', 'Although not generally correct') and that disclosure is to the paper's credit. The Introduction (ST-02) and abstract (ST-01) do not carry it. A consumer reading only the front matter gets a strictly stronger claim than the body supports.

not_a_gap_though_it_looks_like_one.claim: Semaev's argument is sometimes described as leaning on a symmetry that an affine coset shift would destroy. It does not.
not_a_gap_though_it_looks_like_one.evidence: recheck.py RC-2g runs the identical exhibition on an affine descent x_i = v_i + sum_j X_ij alpha_j with random nonzero v_i, in both the 'three shifted subspace variables' and the 'two field variables plus one shifted subspace variable' shapes: bound 4, product degree 3, fall survives every trial.
not_a_gap_though_it_looks_like_one.reason: Squaring over F2 is F2-AFFINE on coordinates, not merely F2-linear, so deg_F2(x^2) = deg_F2(x) is unaffected by a constant shift.
not_a_gap_though_it_looks_like_one.scope_limit: FAKE (multilinear) degree only, at n = 7, one curve parameter, nine random shift triples, multiplier taken to be a field variable exactly as on p.10. Says nothing about the true first fall degree, nothing about d_F4, and nothing about whether any proposition in any paper is true. This task rules on no campaign's action.

proves_too_much_control.object: ST-15 -- the paper's own report that d_F4 generally exceeds 4 when k > ceil(n/m) though the first fall degree is still 4.
proves_too_much_control.object_source: Supplied by the paper itself, not constructed by this task.
proves_too_much_control.outcome: CONTROL FAILS -- the argument survives its own known-false object.
mechanical_evidence: recheck.py RC-2a/RC-2b: sweeping k = 1..n over F_2^5 and F_2^7 with V = {polynomials in alpha of degree < k}, deg S3 = 3, bound = 4, deg(x1*S3) = 3, fall = True at every k. (At k = 1 the fall is deeper, deg 2, from degeneracies in F_2.)
recheck.py RC-2d: at n = 7, m = 3 the exceeded regime is k = 4..7, all covered explicitly by the sweep.
recheck.py RC-2e: random subspaces of dimension 2, 3, n-1, n -- fall survives.
recheck.py RC-2f: the mixed field/subspace shape of system (5) -- fall survives.
recheck.py RC-2g: coset-shifted descents -- fall survives.

recheck.py RC-4: deg_F2(x^a) = popcount(a), verified a = 1..39, because x^(2^i) is F2-linear in the coordinates of x. The entire exhibition is that one fact about the Frobenius, and dim V does not enter it.
what_this_establishes: Assumption 1 (ST-12) is NOT refuted. Its hypothesis k = ceil(n/m) excludes the regime. It is stated correctly.

The JUSTIFICATION offered for Assumption 1 does not distinguish the regime where it is believed from the regime where the author reports it false. The hypothesis that saves the assumption plays no role whatever in the argument for it. Everything the paper offers in support of d_F4 <= 4 at k = ceil(n/m) would equally support d_F4 <= 4 at k = ceil(n/m) + 1, where the paper says it is wrong.

Therefore the first fall degree assumption d_F4 <= d_ff is not merely 'not generally correct' in the abstract (ST-07). It is reported false by this paper's own experiments, on this paper's own family of systems, one parameter step from the regime the FIPS conclusion (ST-03) is drawn in.
proves_too_much_control.what_this_does_not_establish: Nothing here measures d_F4, at any k. The falsity of the conclusion at k > ceil(n/m) is THE PAPER'S OWN REPORT, taken at face value as a statement by the author about his own experiments. This task performed no measurement and makes no claim about the true value of d_F4 anywhere.
proves_too_much_control.contrast_object: The argument is not indiscriminate. Run against the terminal equation ST-10, where the multiplier x1 gives no fall, it CORRECTLY REFUSES (recheck.py RC-1f/g/h) and Semaev flags the refusal in the text. So the argument has a working discriminator along the equation-type axis and NONE along the dim-V axis. That contrast is what makes the k-insensitivity a finding rather than a generic complaint about upper-bound arguments.

neighbouring_literature_used_only_for_ro.note: This task owns no joint on Nagao 2015/984 and adjudicates nothing in it. These are recorded only because the consumed statement reaches this campaign THROUGH them.

items.label: Definition 6, FAKE first fall degree d'_F
The Semaev paragraph: 'In [14], Semaev says ... He uses the true definition of first fall degree.'

could_not_determine.question: Which of ST-02 (S-A, system-level) or ST-11 (S-B, 'at least t-2 of the equations') the campaign treats as the consumed statement.
could_not_determine.why: The campaign's records identify it only by paraphrase inside H-SEMBIN-a7e721's `mechanism` field, with no section, equation, page or line anchor and no provenance marking; and no `citations` block in either H-SEMBIN-a7e721 or EXP-SEMBIN-4fa22c names 2015/310 at all.
could_not_determine.note: Reported rather than resolved, per the card's instruction that such ambiguity is itself the finding.

could_not_determine.question: Whether Semaev's Section 4.4 d_ff (ST-06) is intended over the descent equations alone or over the descents together with the field equations.
could_not_determine.why: The definition is stated for the system (12) and (12) does not include them; the sentence immediately before it (:449-458) does put them into the GROBNER BASIS ideal; and the experiments (:612-613) add them. The text does not say which generating set the d_ff of Assumption 1's justification is taken over.
could_not_determine.impact: Bounded. Adding generators can only lower a first fall degree, so the <= 4 bound transfers either way. It matters because it means ST-07's assumption is never instantiated on one fixed generating set anywhere in the paper.

could_not_determine.question: Which quantity the sentence 'The experiments show it is always 4 again' (ST-10, :598) refers to.
could_not_determine.why: It sits in a first-fall-degree paragraph, but NO EXPERIMENT ANYWHERE IN 2015/310 MEASURES A FIRST FALL DEGREE. Section 4.5.1 measures d_F4 via MAGMA's F4 'step degree' (:629-636) and Tables 1-2 carry a d_F4 column and no d_ff column. I cannot determine whether a separate unreported measurement is meant.
could_not_determine.impact: The paper's one experimental claim about the first fall degree is supported by experiments it describes as measuring a different quantity.

could_not_determine.question: Which reading of Nagao's 'He uses the true definition of first fall degree' (NAGAO-2015-984 :459) is intended.
could_not_determine.why: Reading A -- Semaev STATES the result under the true definition although the available argument gives only the fake bound -- is supported by the placement, immediately after 'Many researchers misunderstand the definition ... and use ... the FAKE version' (:426-428) and immediately before 'it has no problem to use Fake first fall degree instead of use true first fall degree' (:461-463). Reading B -- Semaev correctly uses the true definition -- is also grammatical. The sentence alone does not settle it.
could_not_determine.position_taken: I adopt Reading A and give grounds in report.md J-4b B-6. My own independent reading of Semaev's Section 4.4 definition against his Section 4.5 computation reaches the same place without Nagao, so no finding in this report depends on resolving the sentence.

could_not_determine.question: The '2300 Boolean systems' accounting (ST-13).
could_not_determine.why: Tables 1 and 2 carry 24 rows with t = m (12 in Table 1, 12 in Table 2) at 100 random z each, which is 2400, not 2300 (recheck.py RC-5f/g). The discrepancy is exactly one table row. Which row is uncounted, or whether one row re-reports another (the four n = 17 variants in Table 1 and the n = 17 row of Table 2 are the obvious candidates), is not determinable from the frozen source.
could_not_determine.impact: Minor. Recorded because it is an exact number in the paper.

could_not_determine.question: Whether the `arxiv: 1504.01175` alias in inputs/SEMAEV-2015-310/source_record.yaml is correct.
could_not_determine.why: That record itself flags it as 'NOT independently confirmed in this session'. I did not confirm it either, and no network fetch of arXiv was made.
could_not_determine.impact: None on any finding in this report.

self_limits.hand_check: recheck.py -- 53 assertions, 0 failures, pure Python 3, no third-party dependencies, output captured in recheck.out. It is a SYMBOLIC hand-check of multilinear Boolean degrees over small fields; it measures no runtime, no memory, and no Grobner basis behaviour, and it computes no d_F4.
self_limits.authority: This task rules on what Semaev's argument delivers against what his statement claims, for the joints it owns. It does NOT rule on Semaev's paper as a whole, on Nagao's Proposition 5, on H-SEMBIN-a7e721, or on what the campaign should do -- none of which it can see whole and none of which it has authority over.
